operational_rules_learned_the_hard_way: backend `npm run lint` is `eslint --fix` and rewrites source. Gate on `npx eslint "{src,apps,libs,test}/**/*.ts"` instead.
Run backend unit tests as `TZ=UTC npm run test:unit`; some specs count periods against fixtures and flip under other offsets.
Jest here is v30: the flag is `--testPathPatterns` (plural).
Frontend `npm run test` takes ~9 minutes (628 files). Iterate with `npx vitest run <path>`; run the full suite once before pushing.

A FOREGROUND `sleep` IS BLOCKED in this sandbox, and so are chained short sleeps. To wait for a long job: start it with run_in_background, then a second background job `until [ "$(ps aux | grep -c '[v]itest')" -eq 0 ]; do sleep 15; done`, or the Monitor tool with the same until-loop. The harness notifies you when each exits.

NEVER git stash to check a test fails without the fix WHILE a full-suite run is in flight -- the running suite reads the reverted file mid-run and its result is worthless. Order: per-file revert checks FIRST, then start the full suite, then leave the tree alone until it reports.

The coordination worktree is refreshed with `git reset --hard`, which does NOT delete untracked files -- a newly written DEC survives it. Still, write the DEC and commit it in the same step where you can, rather than leaving it untracked across a fetch.
Pipe a script's output to `head` and you can get a BrokenPipeError traceback AFTER the work already succeeded. Check the effect before believing the traceback.

NEVER write a SHA you have not read from git. Use `git rev-parse <short>`; a full SHA typed from memory is fabricated and lands in the coordination record. I did this once this session and had to correct it.

A MOCK THAT DISCARDS AN ARGUMENT CANNOT TEST THAT ARGUMENT. REV-015 and REV-031 were both invisible because the useNumberFormat mocks were `(amount) => ...`, dropping currencyCode. Same class as a `{ data: [...] }` mock with no `pagination`, which makes fetchAllAccountTransactions throw while a component's swallow hides it. When a finding says 'X is not passed', check the mock honours X before writing the test, and mirror the real fallback (`code || default`).

A CHART TEST'S RECHARTS MOCK IS OFTEN `YAxis: () => null, Tooltip: () => null`, so the tick formatter and tooltip content NEVER RUN and no test can catch a formatting bug in either. Render their output, and have YAxis pass a tick INDEX second, because recharts calls tickFormatter as (value, index): `tickFormatter={formatCurrencyAxis}` by reference silently receives 0 as its currency, and that formatter's `string | number` parameter absorbs it instead of failing. Always wrap.

PREFER A REQUIRED PROP over optional-with-default when threading a currency or any per-entity identity. Required makes tsc enumerate every unfixed call site (it found five in PayoffComparisonChart's test file) and stops the next one reintroducing the bug silently. CLAUDE.md ranks compiler-enforced above scanning test above prose.

'AN EXISTING TEST ALREADY COVERS THIS' IS A CLAIM ABOUT WHICH BRANCH THE TEST RUNS. DateInput.test.tsx has four passing 'touch mode' tests; all sit under the `custom format mode (non-browser format)` describe whose beforeEach sets DD/MM/YYYY, so they exercise touch-FORMATTED mode and say nothing about touch-browser. I nearly disputed half of REV-012 on that basis. Check the enclosing describe's beforeEach and which branch the mode selects before concluding a finding is covered.

DateInput has FOUR modes (touch/desktop x browser/formatted) selected by `getInputMode(dateFormat)` where dateFormat is a USER PREFERENCE. touch-browser has no `if (mode === ...)` branch -- it is the fallback `return` at the end of the component, which is why it is the easiest to miss. A change to any handler contract must be checked in all four.

AN EXISTING TEST ASSERTING THE BEHAVIOUR A FINDING CALLS A BUG IS A FORK, NOT A GREEN LIGHT EITHER WAY. Twice this session: LoanAmortizationReport's 'handles loadTransactions error gracefully' (the defect written down, safe to replace -- CLAUDE.md's 'a failed lookup is not an empty dataset' settles it) versus AmortizationScheduleTable's historical-rate test (no rule settles it, so DEC-20260803-006). The test to apply: does an explicit CLAUDE.md rule or an in-repo pattern decide which artifact is right? If yes, replace the test and say so. If the only evidence is two artifacts disagreeing, escalate.
transactions.status is NULLABLE (schema.sql:274). Never `status != 'VOID'` / `Not(TransactionStatus.VOID)`; use the entity's isVoid getter in JS or `(t.status IS NULL OR t.status != 'VOID')` in SQL.
Reuse an existing translated key across namespaces where the copy is identical. A new en-only errors.json key costs ~36 parity failures.

A nested withScopedDb JOINS the ambient transaction, so an assertXOwned helper opening its own withScopedDb still refuses before the caller's write. Findings written against pre-RLS code will ask for a QueryRunner manager -- there are none left in src/ and lint bans them.
createScopedDbMocks THROWS for an unregistered entity: adding a repository read means registering [Entity, mock] in the spec.

Verify every regression test by actually reverting the fix and re-running. Two of this session's tests pass with or without their fix by design (they pin a boundary the real test moves); only the revert run distinguishes those from vacuous ones, and the finding should say which is which.

vitest `import.meta.glob('/src/...', {query:'?raw', eager:true, import:'default'})` is how the guard tests read source. Pair every scanning assertion with a second one pinning the glob's match count, or a glob that matches nothing passes vacuously forever.
